hints: Focus on what percentage by mass really means, the total mass of nitrogen divided by the total $M_r$ of the whole compound.
Notice that every fertiliser here contains two nitrogen atoms, so $2 \times 14 = 28$ of nitrogen mass, meaning the one with the smallest $M_r$ will win.
Compare the $M_r$ values quickly, especially the heavy sulfate and phosphate groups versus the light $C$ and $O$ in urea, to see which gives the largest fraction.
walkthrough:
**Recall the percentage by mass rule**

Think of it simply as how much of the bag is useful nitrogen. The more heavy extra atoms, the more diluted the nitrogen becomes.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\% \text{ N} = \frac{\text{mass of N atoms}}{M_r \text{ of compound}} \times 100$$

**Count nitrogen in each fertiliser**

Good news, they all have 2 N atoms. So each has $28$ mass units of nitrogen.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3, \text{ (NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4, \text{ (NH}_4)_2\text{HPO}_4, \text{ CO(NH}_2)_2 \text{ all contain } 2\text{N} = 28$$

**Calculate the $M_r$ of each compound**

Use $\text{H}=1, \text{C}=12, \text{N}=14, \text{O}=16, \text{P}=31, \text{S}=32$. The smaller the $M_r$, the larger the nitrogen percentage.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$M_r(\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3) = 80, \quad M_r(\text{(NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4) = 132$$
$$M_r(\text{(NH}_4)_2\text{HPO}_4) = 132, \quad M_r(\text{CO(NH}_2)_2) = 60$$

**Compare and conclude**

With the same $28$ on top, $28/60$ is clearly bigger than $28/80$ or $28/132$. Urea gives about $46.7\%$ nitrogen, the highest.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\% \text{ N in urea} = \frac{28}{60} \times 100 = 46.7\%$$

options.A: Ammonium nitrate has $M_r = 80$ and $\% \text{ N} = 28/80 \times 100 = 35.0\%$. This is high and a common trap because it is a very well known fertiliser, but it is still lower than urea.
options.B: Ammonium sulfate has $M_r = 132$ and $\% \text{ N} = 28/132 \times 100 = 21.2\%$. The sulfate group $\text{SO}_4$ is very heavy, so it dilutes the nitrogen percentage a lot.
options.C: Diammonium hydrogen phosphate also has $M_r = 132$ and $\% \text{ N} = 28/132 \times 100 = 21.2\%$. Like option B, the heavy phosphate group $\text{HPO}_4$ makes the total mass large and the nitrogen fraction small.
options.D: Urea, $\text{CO(NH}_2)_2$, has the smallest $M_r = 60$ and $\% \text{ N} = 28/60 \times 100 = 46.7\%$. With only light C, O and H atoms alongside the two nitrogens, it has the greatest percentage of nitrogen by mass.
